messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most important Texas traffic laws (as of 2024). For full legal detail, consult the Texas Transportation Code or a qualified attorney. | Topic | Key Points | Typical Penalties | |-------|------------|-------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on highways, 35–40 mph in residential zones).
• “No‑limit” roads allow drivers to set their own speed, but must still obey “reasonable and prudent” standards. | • Speeding fines range from $50 to $500 per mph over the limit; higher rates apply for reckless driving. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat unless they’re at least 4 ft 9 in tall. | • Fines up to $200 for seat‑belt violations; higher for minors. | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• First offense: up to 90 days jail, $1,000 fine, 30‑day license suspension.
• Subsequent offenses carry harsher penalties. | • Repeat offenders face longer suspensions, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment, and higher fines. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held cell‑phone use is prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • First offense: $100 fine; second offense: $250 fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop signs require a complete stop; yield signs require slowing and yielding.
• Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | • Failure to yield can result in fines and points on your license. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• No passing within 20 ft of a stopped bus. | • Violations can lead to $300–$600 fines and points. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning or merging.
• “Lane discipline” violations (e.g., weaving) are penalized. | • Fines up to $200; points added to your record. | | **No‑Fault Insurance** | • Texas requires all drivers to carry liability insurance.
• In many cases, each party’s insurer pays for damages regardless of fault. | • Not having coverage can lead to license suspension and civil penalties. | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • Parking in loading zones is prohibited unless you’re loading/unloading.
• Parking in handicap spaces requires a valid permit. | • Fines up to $200; towing may occur. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means proceed only after ensuring it’s safe.
• Yellow lights indicate caution. | • Running red lights can lead to $150–$400 fines and points. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information - **Texas Transportation Code** – Sections 545.001–545.999 cover most traffic rules. - **Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Offers printable handbooks and online resources. - **Legal Aid Websites** – Provide summaries and FAQs tailored to Texas residents. --- #### Want to see recent Texas traffic‑related lawsuits? I can run a quick search for you. Just let me know the year or any specific topic you’re interested in.
